questions.question: Which language should the admin frontend use?
questions.rationale: TypeScript is a strong default for a multi-page admin interface that consumes typed API data.

options.label: TypeScript
options.description: Adds static typing for safer UI and API integration.

options.label: JavaScript
options.description: Uses standard JavaScript without static type checking.

questions.question: Which frontend framework should the admin UI use?
questions.rationale: React is a practical default for an admin SPA and has a mature component ecosystem.

options.label: React
options.description: Component-based UI framework with a broad ecosystem.

options.label: Vue
options.description: Progressive framework with a component-oriented approach.

questions.question: What should the admin frontend include?
questions.answer: Super-admin sign-in and protected navigation; author catalogue search, detail, editing, verification, identifiers, book/audit views, merge preview/merge, and delete; author review queue with keep-separate action; import job history, job/error details, and Open Library/Wikidata import controls; featured homepage configuration and refresh controls; super-admin category management; responsive accessible layouts, loading/empty/error states, and confirmations for destructive actions. Limit actions to existing API capabilities and flag missing API operations rather than assuming new backend endpoints.
questions.rationale: These capabilities map to the existing super-admin-protected author, import, homepage and category APIs.
questions.recommendedChoice: Super-admin sign-in and protected navigation; author catalogue search, detail, editing, verification, identifiers, book/audit views, merge preview/merge, and delete; author review queue with keep-separate action; import job history, job/error details, and Open Library/Wikidata import controls; featured homepage configuration and refresh controls; super-admin category management; responsive accessible layouts, loading/empty/error states, and confirmations for destructive actions. Limit actions to existing API capabilities and flag missing API operations rather than assuming new backend endpoints.

questions.question: Which language does the existing backend use?
questions.rationale: The repository contains a Java 21 Spring Boot backend.

questions.question: Which framework should the backend use?
questions.rationale: The existing API is a custom Java Spring Boot service; retain it and integrate the frontend with its existing REST endpoints.

options.label: Azure Functions
options.description: Azure serverless functions for a new API backend.

questions.question: What backend capabilities should this project use or add?
questions.answer: Use the existing Java Spring Boot REST API and its JWT/super-admin authorization. Integrate with current /admin/author, /admin/author-import, /admin/homepage, and super-admin category-management endpoints. Do not add a new datastore or assume unimplemented admin operations.
questions.rationale: This request is for an admin frontend for an existing backend, not a backend replacement.
questions.recommendedChoice: Use the existing Java Spring Boot REST API and its JWT/super-admin authorization. Integrate with current /admin/author, /admin/author-import, /admin/homepage, and super-admin category-management endpoints. Do not add a new datastore or assume unimplemented admin operations.

questions.question: Which data stores should the project use?
questions.rationale: The existing API already persists marketplace and admin-managed data in MongoDB; the frontend should access it only through the API.

options.label: MongoDB
options.description: Existing document database used by the Rebooked backend.

options.label: No datastore required
options.description: No persistent data store is needed.

questions.question: Will users sign in to access application features?
questions.rationale: The admin interface is restricted to signed-in super-admin users using the existing JWT authentication.

options.label: Yes
options.description: Users sign in before accessing the admin application.

options.label: No
options.description: The application has no sign-in feature.
